statements.impact_statement: CVE-2011-3374 is in the apt-key script's net-update command, which fetched a keyring over the network without verifying the fetched keys against the master keyring. Debian's apt-key never supported net-update because no keyring URI was configured (https://bugs.debian.org/642480), and apt stopped shipping apt-key altogether in 2.9.17 ('Stop installing apt-key, make it a test suite helper', https://sources.debian.org/src/apt/3.0.4/debian/changelog/). This package is built from apt 3.0.4 (earlier published builds from 3.0.3), and neither source tree builds or installs apt-key: cmdline/CMakeLists.txt installs apt, apt-cache, apt-get, apt-config, apt-cdrom, apt-mark and apt-sortpkgs and has no apt-key target (https://sources.debian.org/src/apt/3.0.4/cmdline/CMakeLists.txt/), and the shipped apt package contains no /usr/bin/apt-key (https://packages.debian.org/trixie/amd64/apt/filelist). The vulnerable code is not present in what this package ships. Debian's tracker rates the issue unimportant and records no fixed version (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2011-3374).
